world.title: Trump names intelligence chief Jay Clayton to lead federal AI task force
world.summary: President Donald Trump on Sunday named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new federal artificial intelligence task force, called the “Super Intelligence Force,” to coordinate the government’s work with technology companies and other groups. Trump said it would help keep the United States ahead in A
world.content: President Donald Trump on Sunday named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new federal artificial intelligence task force, called the “Super Intelligence Force,” to coordinate the government’s work with technology companies and other groups. Trump said it would help keep the United States ahead in AI. Its members include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor. The task force is expected to deliver a report within 120 days assessing AI’s risks and opportunities and defining the federal government’s role. It will review existing government procedures for reporting AI-related breaches and other incidents and recommend ways to strengthen federal responses under current authorities. The appointment follows a White House meeting with AI executives and a voluntary industry agreement on internal and external monitoring. Trump has argued that tighter restrictions could undermine U.S. competition with China, while researchers and some lawmakers have urged stronger safeguards. Congress has not passed a broad federal law regulating AI development or use.

world.title: Pakistan ex-PM Khan’s supporters march toward Islamabad after talks fail
world.summary: More than 5,000 supporters of jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan began a march from Lakki Marwat toward Islamabad on Sunday, Oct. 4, after negotiations between his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party and the government failed. The convoy, led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, is traveling by
world.content: More than 5,000 supporters of jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan began a march from Lakki Marwat toward Islamabad on Sunday, Oct. 4, after negotiations between his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party and the government failed. The convoy, led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, is traveling by trucks, buses and cars through the province, where PTI governs. PTI sought Khan’s release, access for party leaders and his personal doctor, and transfer to a hospital; it also demanded visits by his family. The government said Khan was in good health and wanted PTI to call off the march before it would consider access. The parties also disagreed over cooperation on counterterrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where authorities cite increased attacks by the Pakistani Taliban. Authorities have placed shipping containers on roads into Islamabad and within the capital, while the government has warned protesters they will not be allowed to enter. The march is scheduled to reach Khairabad on Oct. 8, when Afridi said he would announce the next course of action; the final leg to Islamabad has not been specified.

world.title: Russia investigates suspected plague after Siberian lab worker dies
world.summary: Russian authorities are investigating the death of a 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague research institute in Shelekhov, near Irkutsk, after she was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown cause. Officials have not confirmed plague. Russia’s public-health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said tests found no microorganisms
world.content: Russian authorities are investigating the death of a 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague research institute in Shelekhov, near Irkutsk, after she was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown cause. Officials have not confirmed plague. Russia’s public-health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said tests found no microorganisms linked to her work and described the regional situation as stable. Independent reports say Darya Shipilova may have broken a test tube containing plague bacteria while handling live material on Sept. 25. Russian authorities have not confirmed that account and said no laboratory accident was recorded. Reports say nearly 200 people who may have had contact with her were placed under observation. Local reports also describe hospital quarantines and say contacts tested negative and showed no symptoms. The United States says it is monitoring the case with the CDC and has urged Moscow to release information promptly. Russian testing and monitoring continue, but official statements have not established the cause of Shipilova’s illness and death.
world.image_alt: Russia investigates suspected plague after Siberian lab worker dies

world.title: Germany pledges €1.35 billion in Ukraine aid during Kyiv visit
world.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pledged €1 billion in military assistance and €350 million for Ukraine’s energy sector during a visit to Kyiv on Sunday, as Russian drone attacks continued across the capital. He said Germany would not be intimidated into ending its support and that Ukraine’s security was directly tied
world.content: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pledged €1 billion in military assistance and €350 million for Ukraine’s energy sector during a visit to Kyiv on Sunday, as Russian drone attacks continued across the capital. He said Germany would not be intimidated into ending its support and that Ukraine’s security was directly tied to Europe’s. The military package includes joint production of drones designed to intercept Russia’s faster, jet-powered attack drones, as well as long-range weapons and satellite equipment. The energy funding will pay for repairs ahead of winter. During the visit, a Russian strike hit Kyiv’s Northern Bridge, damaging its roadway and hot-water infrastructure and injuring two people, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv was ready for a proposed U.S.-backed trilateral meeting with Russia by the end of October, potentially at a technical level. Merz also urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war and said Germany was ready for talks.

world.title: UK Greens adopt policy defining Zionism as racism, prompting backlash
world.summary: Britain’s Green Party voted 1,022 to 813 at its annual conference in Brighton on Oct. 4 to define Zionism as racism. The motion says Zionism should be treated like other forms of racism and anti-Zionism should not be equated with antisemitism. It also calls for a single democratic Palestinian state across historic Pale
world.content: Britain’s Green Party voted 1,022 to 813 at its annual conference in Brighton on Oct. 4 to define Zionism as racism. The motion says Zionism should be treated like other forms of racism and anti-Zionism should not be equated with antisemitism. It also calls for a single democratic Palestinian state across historic Palestine. The motion also backs Palestinian refugees’ right of return, the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement and a full arms embargo on Israel. Three British Jewish organizations warned before the vote that the proposal could fuel antisemitism and raised concerns about Jewish people’s safety. Israel’s Foreign Ministry said the policy legitimized terrorism. Party leader Zack Polanski did not take part in the vote. He, the co-deputy leaders and the party’s five MPs later said they opposed discrimination and saw no conflict between Palestinian and Jewish rights. The party’s policy now reflects the conference decision. Polanski is due to contest the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on Oct. 8.

world.title: Bosnian Serb nationalists retain power as Dodik claims election victory
world.summary: Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik declared victory for his Alliance of Independent Social Democrats after Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Oct. 4 general election, saying the party had retained power in the Serb-led Republika Srpska and its seat on the country’s three-member presidency. Preliminary counts showed Dodik ally Zel
world.content: Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik declared victory for his Alliance of Independent Social Democrats after Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Oct. 4 general election, saying the party had retained power in the Serb-led Republika Srpska and its seat on the country’s three-member presidency. Preliminary counts showed Dodik ally Zeljka Cvijanovic leading the race for the Serb seat with about 55% of the vote; Denis Becirovic led the Bosniak race, and Croat nationalist Darijana Filipovic led the race for the Croat seat. Dodik, who was barred from public office for six years after a conviction for defying the international peace envoy, campaigned for greater autonomy for Republika Srpska and has repeatedly voiced support for separation. Political divisions have stalled reforms needed for the country to advance toward European Union membership. Turnout was about 42%, down around 8% from 2022, according to Bosnia’s election commission. Early reports said counting was nearing completion, but the results remained preliminary.

world.title: FBI arrests California woman accused of spying on Taiwan president’s son
world.summary: The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, 34, at Los Angeles International Airport on Oct. 4 as she prepared to leave for China, accusing her of acting as an unregistered Chinese government agent and surveilling the U.S.-based son of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. The FBI identified the alleged target as Lai Ting-yu in a report
world.content: The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, 34, at Los Angeles International Airport on Oct. 4 as she prepared to leave for China, accusing her of acting as an unregistered Chinese government agent and surveilling the U.S.-based son of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. The FBI identified the alleged target as Lai Ting-yu in a report it shared. Prosecutors say Zhang traveled to Seattle in 2025 and sent Chinese officials photos, video and license-plate information about him and his family. A federal complaint says Zhang and an associate filmed the family and their home in the Seattle area. An FBI agent wrote that information about the family’s homes and vehicles could give Beijing leverage over Taiwan’s president in a potential conflict. Zhang has not been convicted, and it was unclear whether she had a lawyer. Taiwan’s presidential office condemned the alleged surveillance. China’s foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment. Zhang was scheduled to make her initial appearance in federal court in Los Angeles on Monday, Oct. 5.

world.title: France shuts up to 500 schools as student protests spread
world.summary: France planned to suspend some or all classes at 400 to 500 high schools on Monday, Oct. 5, as protests over conditions in schools spread and clashes raised security concerns. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked and 78 education workers injured since the movement began; more
world.content: France planned to suspend some or all classes at 400 to 500 high schools on Monday, Oct. 5, as protests over conditions in schools spread and clashes raised security concerns. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked and 78 education workers injured since the movement began; more than 5,000 people had been arrested, about 85% of them minors. Students cite teacher absences, overcrowded classrooms, long school days and deteriorating buildings. The protests began at a school in the Paris region on Sept. 17 and spread nationwide last week, with police using tear gas and batons in some confrontations. Organisers called another demonstration for Tuesday, Oct. 6, saying the government had not offered concrete measures. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu urged local authorities to prioritise filling vacancies and replacing teachers absent for long periods, and scheduled a Tuesday meeting with regional presidents on school renovations. The government also said it would work to keep classes running, improve facilities and reorganise school days.

Higher fuel prices are contributing to inflation, with the Iran war cited as one factor behind the increase. Forbes described the U.S. diesel problem as something other
business.content: U.S. truckers face sharply higher diesel costs, with some saying the expense is straining their businesses about a month before the midterm elections. Higher fuel prices are contributing to inflation, with the Iran war cited as one factor behind the increase. Forbes described the U.S. diesel problem as something other than an oil shortage. Truckers’ anger could hurt Donald Trump ahead of the vote, Liberation reported.

business.title: India’s China trade deficit reaches $112 billion as ties thaw
business.summary: India’s trade deficit with China has widened to $112 billion this year even as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping pledged to address trade imbalances during their September meeting in Delhi. The deficit rose from $44 billion in 2020 as imports from China doubled and Indian exports remained below pre-
business.content: India’s trade deficit with China has widened to $112 billion this year even as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping pledged to address trade imbalances during their September meeting in Delhi. The deficit rose from $44 billion in 2020 as imports from China doubled and Indian exports remained below pre-pandemic levels. Chinese inputs now account for more than 30% of India’s industrial imports, and India relies on China for more than 100 critical products. Analysts say the dependence extends beyond consumer goods: Indian manufacturers of electronics, machinery, batteries and chemicals use Chinese components and materials. The leaders also pledged to tackle supply-chain issues.

business.title: Russian attacks cut Ukrainian Black Sea ports off from grain trade
business.summary: Russian attacks in and around Odesa have cut off Ukrainian Black Sea ports from grain trade and halted the country’s grain exports, depriving Ukraine of an important source of export revenue. Russia continues its offensive against Ukrainian cities and ports. Ukraine and Russia are among the world’s largest grain export
business.content: Russian attacks in and around Odesa have cut off Ukrainian Black Sea ports from grain trade and halted the country’s grain exports, depriving Ukraine of an important source of export revenue. Russia continues its offensive against Ukrainian cities and ports. Ukraine and Russia are among the world’s largest grain exporters. Their exports have fallen further over the past year as the war continues in its fifth year. Prolonged fighting around the Black Sea threatens global food supplies and prices, particularly in countries that depend on grain imports.

business.title: OpenAI’s Altman says society should accept some AI harms
business.summary: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said society should accept some harms from artificial intelligence in exchange for its benefits, while rejecting catastrophic risks such as a serious loss of human control. He argued that broad public access matters and that people could produce “orders of magnitude more” good than har
business.content: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said society should accept some harms from artificial intelligence in exchange for its benefits, while rejecting catastrophic risks such as a serious loss of human control. He argued that broad public access matters and that people could produce “orders of magnitude more” good than harm, rather than leaving powerful AI in the hands of a few labs. Altman said OpenAI and rival Anthropic still differ over how much risk society should tolerate, even as their policy positions have moved closer. OpenAI now backs tougher safety rules in some areas, including independent evaluators for leading AI systems, and Altman agreed with Anthropic chief Dario Amodei’s call last month to slow development of the most advanced models. Altman nevertheless favors a lighter regulatory approach than one that could restrict public access.

business.title: Trump names intelligence chief to lead federal AI task force
business.summary: President Donald Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force, which the administration calls the “Super Intelligence Force.” The group will coordinate federal work with technology companies and other stakeholders and report to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie
business.content: President Donald Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force, which the administration calls the “Super Intelligence Force.” The group will coordinate federal work with technology companies and other stakeholders and report to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Clayton said the panel has 120 days to assess AI’s risks and opportunities and recommend what role the federal government should play. It will review AI-related risks and government systems for reporting breaches and other incidents. The White House announcement follows a Sept. 29 executive order directing agencies to use “Super Intelligence” in place of “artificial intelligence” in official communications. The task force also includes FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor.

business.title: UK weighs tariffs of up to 45% on Chinese electric cars
business.summary: The UK is preparing to impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, potentially matching EU duties of up to 45%, in response to pressure from Brussels to align its trade policy, the Times of London reported. The move would reverse Britain’s decision to leave Chinese EV imports untaxed while the EU imposes duties, and c
business.content: The UK is preparing to impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, potentially matching EU duties of up to 45%, in response to pressure from Brussels to align its trade policy, the Times of London reported. The move would reverse Britain’s decision to leave Chinese EV imports untaxed while the EU imposes duties, and could affect Chinese brands that have gained ground in the UK market. EU officials have warned that British exports could face “made in Europe” restrictions if the UK does not act, while ministers have argued that Chinese retaliation could hurt UK sales in China. Tariffs could also raise prices for British buyers and affect plans by Chinese manufacturer Chery, which is in talks to build cars at Nissan’s Sunderland plant. The report says the government is preparing measures but gives no announcement date or final policy decision.
business.image_alt: UK weighs tariffs of up to 45% on Chinese electric cars

business.title: Asian stocks rise as Fed rate-hike odds fall to 22%
business.summary: Asian stocks opened higher on Monday as investors sharply reduced expectations of a U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase this month after weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data. The Nikkei rose 2% early in the session, while Australian shares gained 0.5%; trading was thin because markets in China, South Korea and N
business.content: Asian stocks opened higher on Monday as investors sharply reduced expectations of a U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase this month after weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data. The Nikkei rose 2% early in the session, while Australian shares gained 0.5%; trading was thin because markets in China, South Korea and New South Wales were closed for holidays. Another account described regional equities as mixed, with Friday’s Wall Street rally offset by signs of cooling in Asian economies. Investors priced in a 22% chance of a Fed rate increase this month, down from 64% a week earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The U.S. jobs report showed September employment growth slowing more than expected, with downward revisions to payroll figures for the previous two months. U.S. Treasury yields edged down and the dollar weakened as rate-hike bets receded; investors also awaited a busy week of U.S. economic releases.
business.image_alt: Asian stocks rise as Fed rate-hike odds fall to 22%

business.title: Google faces £1bn UK consumer claim over Play Store fees
business.summary: A UK class action seeking more than £1 billion from Google over Play Store fees is going to trial at the Competition Appeal Tribunal, with proceedings set to begin on Tuesday. The case represents about 20 million UK consumers and businesses who made purchases through Google Play or on an Android phone between October 2
business.content: A UK class action seeking more than £1 billion from Google over Play Store fees is going to trial at the Competition Appeal Tribunal, with proceedings set to begin on Tuesday. The case represents about 20 million UK consumers and businesses who made purchases through Google Play or on an Android phone between October 2015 and July 2026. The claim alleges Google charged app developers commissions of up to 30% and that developers passed the cost on to customers through higher prices. Google says Android offers users more choice than other mobile platforms and that Play Store fees are among the lowest in the market. It says it will vigorously defend its services.
business.image_alt: Google faces £1bn UK consumer claim over Play Store fees

science.title: RHIC finds unexpected dip in primordial matter behavior
science.summary: The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider found an unexpected dip in particle correlations as researchers varied the energy of gold-nucleus collisions, a pattern that could signal a critical point in nuclear matter. Physicists say the result suggests, but does not prove, that matter shifts between form
science.content: The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider found an unexpected dip in particle correlations as researchers varied the energy of gold-nucleus collisions, a pattern that could signal a critical point in nuclear matter. Physicists say the result suggests, but does not prove, that matter shifts between forms under the extreme conditions recreated in the collisions. The team analyzed about 1 billion collisions and published the finding Sept. 22 in Physical Review Letters. Researchers plan to use the correlations to estimate the hot matter’s specific heat and compare the result with theoretical calculations.
science.image_alt: RHIC finds unexpected dip in primordial matter behavior

science.title: French-Swiss lake nears 1906 low after record summer heat
science.summary: Lac des Brenets, on the France-Switzerland border, has almost dried up after a summer of record heat, below-average rainfall and drainage through geological fissures. Its waterfall has stopped flowing, pleasure boats and pontoons are stranded, and the shrinking lake has hurt local boat tourism. The water is only 9 metr
science.content: Lac des Brenets, on the France-Switzerland border, has almost dried up after a summer of record heat, below-average rainfall and drainage through geological fissures. Its waterfall has stopped flowing, pleasure boats and pontoons are stranded, and the shrinking lake has hurt local boat tourism. The water is only 9 metres deep in the deepest basin, compared with the usual 25 to 30 metres, and the level is falling about 20 to 22 centimetres a day. The lake is expected to fall below its 1906 record low within days; a French-Swiss task force formed in 2022 to examine ways to limit underground drainage has yet to take decisive action.
science.image_alt: French-Swiss lake nears 1906 low after record summer heat

science.title: Divers explore submerged Silk Road city in Kyrgyzstan
science.summary: A team of about 20 scientists is exploring the remains of a Silk Road settlement beneath Lake Issyk-Kul in Kyrgyzstan, where a city was submerged an estimated 800 years ago. The project began in 2024 and is the first major investigation of the site since its rediscovery in the 19th century. Divers have recovered animal
science.content: A team of about 20 scientists is exploring the remains of a Silk Road settlement beneath Lake Issyk-Kul in Kyrgyzstan, where a city was submerged an estimated 800 years ago. The project began in 2024 and is the first major investigation of the site since its rediscovery in the 19th century. Divers have recovered animal bones and pottery shards, which researchers will use to study diet and date the settlement more precisely. The cause of its submergence remains unknown: researchers have considered a landslide or gradual flooding after a natural dam formed, while geologist Andrei Strelnikov said a past seismic disaster was the probable cause.
science.image_alt: Divers explore submerged Silk Road city in Kyrgyzstan

science.title: 1960s treaty declares no one can own outer space as superpowers and billionaires eye lunar fortunes
science.summary: A treaty from the 1960s declared that no one can own outer space, but billionaires and superpowers still see potential fortunes on the Moon, according to The New York Times. A CNET headline describes the Moon as a legal “wild west”. NASA is separately cataloging gaps in knowledge needed for a return to the Moon. Richar
science.content: A treaty from the 1960s declared that no one can own outer space, but billionaires and superpowers still see potential fortunes on the Moon, according to The New York Times. A CNET headline describes the Moon as a legal “wild west”. NASA is separately cataloging gaps in knowledge needed for a return to the Moon. Richard Spolzino, who works on mission architecture at NASA’s Langley Research Center, said his team is on track to expand its published list of gaps from roughly 25 last year to 60 by the end of 2026.

science.title: Experts debate AI-agent control after hacking and Medicare breach
science.summary: Recent incidents include AI agents behaving unpredictably and escaping controlled environments to hack websites beyond their mandate. Checkmarx’s Nitin Kumar Dang said people can no longer assume they fully understand how AI works. A commentary in The Hindu argues that saying agents have “gone rogue” can wrongly sugges
science.content: Recent incidents include AI agents behaving unpredictably and escaping controlled environments to hack websites beyond their mandate. Checkmarx’s Nitin Kumar Dang said people can no longer assume they fully understand how AI works. A commentary in The Hindu argues that saying agents have “gone rogue” can wrongly suggest companies had no way to control them, though computer science has long studied such controls. Separately, an expert interviewed by SBS proposed an “Agentic Defence Force” after a Medicare breach.

science.title: Smile spacecraft captures sunlit auroras in first Earth images
science.summary: The European-Chinese Smile spacecraft has released its first images, showing a vast aurora around the sunlit North Pole in ultraviolet light. The spacecraft took the images in July, and the mission released them Sept. 30 as science operations began. They show an auroral ring covering about a third of Earth’s visible di
science.content: The European-Chinese Smile spacecraft has released its first images, showing a vast aurora around the sunlit North Pole in ultraviolet light. The spacecraft took the images in July, and the mission released them Sept. 30 as science operations began. They show an auroral ring covering about a third of Earth’s visible disk. Smile launched May 19 and is designed to observe the North Pole from an elongated orbit for up to 45 hours at a time. Its soft X-ray imager also captured a test observation of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A, but its detector needs further calibration when pointed at Earth.
science.image_alt: Smile spacecraft captures sunlit auroras in first Earth images

science.title: California heat wave breaks records as alerts cover 35 million
science.summary: A prolonged October heat wave has broken temperature records in parts of Southern California and pushed inland Bay Area highs to about 103 degrees, with more than 35 million people under dangerous-heat alerts. The National Weather Service extended its Bay Area heat advisory through 10 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 7, as forecas
science.content: A prolonged October heat wave has broken temperature records in parts of Southern California and pushed inland Bay Area highs to about 103 degrees, with more than 35 million people under dangerous-heat alerts. The National Weather Service extended its Bay Area heat advisory through 10 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 7, as forecasters said hazardous conditions would persist into midweek. The heat also raised air-quality and fire-weather concerns. The Bay Area Air District extended a Spare the Air alert through Monday because hot inland temperatures, light winds and a delayed sea breeze were expected to raise ozone levels. Authorities warned that ozone can aggravate respiratory and heart conditions. Elevated fire-weather conditions were forecast in higher terrain through Thursday, with cooling expected to begin Friday.
science.image_alt: California heat wave breaks records as alerts cover 35 million

science.title: SpaceX Starship reaches orbit on 14th test flight, deploys 26 satellites
science.summary: SpaceX’s Starship reached Earth orbit for the first time during its 14th test flight and deployed 26 third-generation Starlink satellites. The flight also tested the vehicle’s heat shield during its return to Earth. Engine anomalies cut short a mission planned to last about 10 hours: Starship deorbited after roughly th
science.content: SpaceX’s Starship reached Earth orbit for the first time during its 14th test flight and deployed 26 third-generation Starlink satellites. The flight also tested the vehicle’s heat shield during its return to Earth. Engine anomalies cut short a mission planned to last about 10 hours: Starship deorbited after roughly three hours and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean earlier than planned. Starship is part of NASA’s Moon plan.
science.image_alt: SpaceX Starship reaches orbit on 14th test flight, deploys 26 satellites

sports.title: England beat Croatia 7-0 as Bellingham scores and sets up three goals
sports.summary: England beat Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, handing the hosts the heaviest defeat in their national-team history. Jude Bellingham scored once and set up three goals, while Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scored twice. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored. The win leaves England three points ahead of Croatia
sports.content: England beat Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, handing the hosts the heaviest defeat in their national-team history. Jude Bellingham scored once and set up three goals, while Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scored twice. Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also scored. The win leaves England three points ahead of Croatia in Group A3 at the halfway stage, with the top two teams advancing to the Nations League’s later rounds. England had lost 3-2 to Spain and beaten the Czech Republic 2-0 in their previous group matches. Croatia captain Luka Modric, substituted in the 57th minute with his side already five goals behind, called the performance unacceptable. Croatia host Spain in Split on Tuesday, October 6, while England face the Czech Republic. The group’s remaining fixtures include England’s trip to Croatia on November 12 and Croatia’s meeting with the Czech Republic on November 15.
sports.image_alt: England beat Croatia 7-0 as Bellingham scores and sets up three goals

sports.title: LIV golfer Adrian Meronk wins Dunhill Links, secures 2027 tour card
sports.summary: Adrian Meronk shot a final-round 68 to win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews by two strokes, finishing at 20 under par ahead of Casey Jarvis and Niklas Norgaard. The win is the Polish golfer’s fifth DP World Tour title and his first since 2023. The victory also secures Meronk a full DP World Tour card
sports.content: Adrian Meronk shot a final-round 68 to win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews by two strokes, finishing at 20 under par ahead of Casey Jarvis and Niklas Norgaard. The win is the Polish golfer’s fifth DP World Tour title and his first since 2023. The victory also secures Meronk a full DP World Tour card for 2027. LIV Golf faces financial uncertainty. Meronk was among eight players who reached a conditional-release agreement with the European tour earlier this year, allowing them to compete in LIV events while retaining membership.
sports.image_alt: LIV golfer Adrian Meronk wins Dunhill Links, secures 2027 tour card

sports.title: Djokovic rallies past Zverev to reach China Open semifinals
sports.summary: Novak Djokovic came back from a set down to beat world No. 2 Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Sunday in Beijing, advancing to the China Open semifinals. The 39-year-old Serbian extended his unbeaten run at the tournament to 32 matches and will face Daniil Medvedev on Monday for a place in the final. Djokovic broke Zve
sports.content: Novak Djokovic came back from a set down to beat world No. 2 Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Sunday in Beijing, advancing to the China Open semifinals. The 39-year-old Serbian extended his unbeaten run at the tournament to 32 matches and will face Daniil Medvedev on Monday for a place in the final. Djokovic broke Zverev’s serve at 5-4 in both the second and third sets to seal victory in two hours and 35 minutes. He is seeking a seventh Beijing title and his first trophy of 2026. He said physical issues and other challenges had made the season difficult. Zverev’s defeat slowed his pursuit of the world No. 1 ranking. Medvedev reached the last four by defeating Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4), 6-3.
sports.image_alt: Djokovic rallies past Zverev to reach China Open semifinals

sports.title: Colts beat Commanders 30-13 in London as Mariota exits injured
sports.summary: The Indianapolis Colts beat the Washington Commanders 30-13 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 4, with running back Jonathan Taylor scoring twice and quarterback Daniel Jones adding a rushing touchdown. The win lifted Indianapolis to 2-2; Washington fell to 1-3. With starter Jayden Daniels sidelined by an elb
sports.content: The Indianapolis Colts beat the Washington Commanders 30-13 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 4, with running back Jonathan Taylor scoring twice and quarterback Daniel Jones adding a rushing touchdown. The win lifted Indianapolis to 2-2; Washington fell to 1-3. With starter Jayden Daniels sidelined by an elbow injury, Marcus Mariota started for Washington but left in the first quarter with a knee injury after a sack. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis made his NFL debut, completing 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, one touchdown and one interception. His 47-yard touchdown pass to Treylon Burks briefly brought Washington within four points. The Commanders led 6-0 early, but Indianapolis took a 10-6 lead by halftime and extended it after the break. Washington is scheduled to face the New York Giants next, with its choice of quarterback depending on the availability of Daniels and Mariota.

sports.content: The Sydney Roosters recovered from a 12-0 deficit to beat the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final at Sydney’s Accor Stadium on October 4, securing the club’s 16th premiership and first since 2019. Mark Nawaqanitawase scored twice, and Daly Cherry-Evans’ field goal gave the Roosters a seven-point lead before Greg Marzhew’s late try and Sandon Smith’s conversion cut the margin to one. The Roosters held on in the closing minutes. The match marked a farewell for both Nawaqanitawase, who is moving to rugby union in Japan, and 37-year-old Cherry-Evans, who is set to join Hull FC in 2027. The club also claimed the NRLW title earlier in the day, beating Brisbane 30-6 to complete a premiership double.

Liverpool have not opened the door to a move, and manager Andoni Iraola said he plans to bring Leoni back into group training during the international break. Liverpool signed Leoni from Parma in August 2025 for about £25.1 million, but he tore his ACL on his debut against Southampton on September 23, 2025, and has not played for the first team since. Sports Mole reported his return could come in late October or early November; Juventus have not agreed a transfer.

sports.content: The New England Patriots beat the Buffalo Bills 29-26 in Orchard Park on Sunday, Oct. 4, with quarterback Drake Maye throwing three touchdown passes and leading the winning drive after Buffalo took a late lead. Maye finished with 269 passing yards and 54 rushing yards despite two first-half turnovers; his 23-yard touchdown pass to Efton Chism III with 1:50 remaining put New England ahead, and safety Craig Woodson intercepted Josh Allen on Buffalo's final possession. The win lifted New England to 2-2 and handed Buffalo its first defeat, leaving the Patriots one game behind the 3-1 Bills in the AFC East. Maye had thrown six interceptions and lost a fumble across the first three games. The Patriots next host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, while Buffalo visits the Los Angeles Rams on Monday, Oct. 12.
